checklist.notes: The travel request frame is broadly A2.1, but key instructions and models rely on unsupported language such as ‘confirm the 5:20 departure’, ‘information needs’, ‘unfamiliar listener’s attention’, and ‘fuller request’.
The friend model ‘check 5:20’ lacks a natural object or clause for check and is not a reliable lexical pattern to teach.
Because ‘check 5:20’ is central model language, the informal request is noticeably non-idiomatic even though the staff exchange is otherwise natural.
No suspicious unexplained reuse was found within the supplied artifacts; no external originality search was performed.
The lesson reviews the established help function and word stress and introduces only the authorized assessment and politeness concepts with phoneme/syllable prerequisites.
All content is English and embedded IDs stay within the exact request and context-only closure.

findings.description: Section 2 teaches ‘Help me find Gate 4 and check 5:20, please.’ In this context, bare ‘check 5:20’ is lexically incomplete/non-idiomatic: the listener needs to check the departure or check whether the service leaves at that time.
findings.recommendation: Use ‘Help me find Gate 4 and check the 5:20 departure, please’ or, more explicitly, ‘check whether it leaves at 5:20.’

findings.description: Core learner directions combine nominalized and metapragmatic language above A2.1 without scaffolding. The learner must decode ‘confirm a departure’, ‘information needs’, and a ‘fuller request’ before practising a simple help exchange.
findings.recommendation: Retain the travel setting but state each need with short A2 language, explain confirm in context, and reduce the metapragmatic prose.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
